finding.claim: The /fetch handler passes an unvalidated, attacker-controlled URL to http.Get and returns the response body to the client, enabling full-response SSRF to internal hosts and cloud metadata endpoints.
finding.source: r.URL.Query().Get("target") at main.go:15 (query string of GET /fetch)
finding.sink: http.Get(target) at main.go:16; response copied to client via io.Copy at main.go:22

trace.note: target read from query string, no processing
response body streamed back to the caller

finding.guards_checked: None. No scheme check, host allowlist, IP/private-range block, port restriction, or redirect control on this path.

verdict.guard_found: none on the /fetch path. The allowlist map at main.go:9-12 is only consulted in safeFetch (main.go:27), which is registered on a separate route (/safe, main.go:42). fetch (main.go:14-23) passes the raw query value to http.Get at main.go:16 with no scheme, host, IP, or redirect check.
verdict.reason:
main.go:41 routes /fetch to fetch, which reads the unauthenticated query parameter `target` (main.go:15), passes it unchecked to http.Get (main.go:16), and streams the full response body back to the caller (main.go:22), so an attacker can reach internal hosts and metadata endpoints; the only validated path is the separate /safe handler at main.go:25-38.</reason>
</invoke>

finding.claim: The /safe handler's hostname allowlist can be bypassed if an allowed host redirects to an internal or metadata address, because Go's default client follows redirects and the allowlist is checked only on the original URL.
finding.source: r.URL.Query().Get("target") at main.go:26 (query string of GET /safe)
finding.sink: http.Get(u.String()) at main.go:31; response copied to client at main.go:37

trace.note: allowed[u.Hostname()] exact-match check against images.example.org and docs.example.org; non-match returns 403
http.Get follows up to 10 redirects by default; no CheckRedirect re-validation
final response body returned to the client

finding.guards_checked: Parse error handling (u not dereferenced when err != nil, no nil deref); exact Hostname() match (handles userinfo and port correctly); u.String() round-trip (no parser differential). Missing: redirect validation, IP/private-range blocking. Scheme restriction is effectively enforced by Go (non-HTTP schemes rejected). Exploitability depends on whether an allowed host (placeholder example.org names) can be induced to redirect internally.

verdict.guard_found: main.go:27 `if err != nil || !allowed[u.Hostname()]` is an exact-match membership check on the parsed hostname against the allowed map (images.example.org, docs.example.org), returning 403 on mismatch before the sink at main.go:31.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (main.go:42, 26, 27, 31, 37 all match the described behavior) and the source at main.go:26 is attacker-controlled, but the exact hostname membership check at main.go:27 is a closing guard under the verification rules, so the finding does not stand. The redirect-following concern is real as a hardening gap, since the allowlist is only applied to the original URL and http.Get follows up to 10 redirects, but it depends on an allowed host being induced to redirect internally, which the candidate itself marks as unestablished.
